prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Added `heading_offset` (whole number 0–5, default 0; other values raise ValueError) to `Markdown`/`markdown()`, plus `--heading-offset N` on the command line. A new `heading_offset` treeprocessor at priority 6 moves every h1–h6 in the tree down by the offset, up to h6. This covers hash, underline and md_in_html headings. It runs just before `toc` (priority 5), so the toc tokens and `toc_depth` use the shifted levels, and any toc `baselevel` adds on top of the offset. Raw HTML passed through unchanged is not shifted, and a treeprocessor added by an extension that runs before priority 6 sees the original levels. Documentation, changelog and tests are added; all 1146 tests pass. flake8 isn't installed, so I only checked the 119-character line limit by hand.
